---
title: "A bar chart race, with no new API"
description: "transition_states() over a rank column turns mark_bar() into a bar chart race: each bar is keyed to its country by its fill, so bars slide past each other as their ranks change, on frozen scales."
categories: [Animation]
image: figs/bar-race-poster.png
---

```{r}
#| include: false
source("_helper.R")
```

A bar chart race is a ranking that reorders itself over time. There is no
`mark_race()`: it falls out of `mark_bar()`, `coord_flip()` and
`transition_states()`, because the tween engine matches each bar to *the same
country* in the next state and interpolates its position as well as its length. When
two countries swap rank, their bars slide past each other.

The one thing the data has to carry is the rank. Bar position comes from the `x`
encoding, so ranking within each year and mapping `x = rank` is what makes bars move;
map `x = country` instead and you get twelve years of bars growing in place.

```{r}
library(gapminder)

g <- transform(as.data.frame(gapminder), gdp = pop * gdpPercap / 1e9)
biggest <- head(g[g$year == 2007, ][order(-g$gdp[g$year == 2007]), "country"], 10)

d <- g[g$country %in% biggest, c("country", "year", "gdp")]
d$country <- droplevels(d$country)
d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(d, d$year), function(s) {
  s$rank <- rank(s$gdp, ties.method = "first")
  s[order(-s$rank), ] # rows in rank order: the tween does not care
}))

head(d[d$year == 1952, ], 3)
```

Ten countries, twelve five-year steps, and a rank from 1 (smallest) to 10 (largest)
recomputed inside each year. The rows of each year are in rank order, so a country sits
on a different row from one year to the next. That does not matter: a bar's identity
is its group, and with no `group` or `data_id` given, the group is the combination of
the layer's discrete mappings, here `fill = country`. The text layer is keyed the same
way, by its discrete `label = country`.

```{r}
a <- vplot(d, width = 7, height = 4.5, dpi = 150) |>
  mark_bar(x = rank, y = gdp, fill = country) |>
  mark_text(x = rank, y = gdp + 150, label = country, hjust = 0, size = 10) |>
  coord_flip() |>
  guides(fill = "none") |>
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 16000)) |>
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank()) |>
  labs(title = "Total GDP of the ten largest economies of 2007, in {closest_state}",
       x = NULL, y = "billions of 1990 dollars") |>
  transition_states(year, transition_length = 2, state_length = 1, wrap = FALSE) |>
  animate(nframes = 330, fps = 25)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
dir.create("figs", showWarnings = FALSE)
anim_save("figs/bar-race.svg", a)
knitr::include_graphics("figs/bar-race.svg")
```

```{r}
#| include: false
# The listing card: the animation's own last frame.
anim_frame("figs/bar-race-poster.png", a, scale = 100 / a@dpi)
```

China starts seventh of the ten and takes second place off Japan in 2002. Japan had
climbed to second in 1972 and held it until then. India sits eighth as late as 1997,
then passes Italy, France, the United Kingdom and Germany to reach fourth by 2007. The
United States never moves. Labels ride their bars, so you can follow one country through
the reshuffling instead of re-reading the axis every time the order changes.

## What the engine is doing

Bars interpolate on two channels at once. Length follows `gdp`, and position follows
`rank`, so a country whose rank changes by one slides one slot while its bar grows. The
scales were trained once across all twelve years and frozen, which is why the axis never
jumps: 1952 is drawn against the same 16000-billion axis as 2007, and the growth is
legible as growth rather than as a rescaling.

`transition_length` and `state_length` set the rhythm. With 2:1 and `wrap = FALSE`,
the 330 frames give each of the eleven moves about 20 frames and hold each year for
about 10, so the overtakes are visible and the ranking is readable at rest. `wrap =
FALSE` ends the animation on 2007 instead of adding a twelfth move that slides every
bar back to its 1952 place. The file still loops, so playback cuts from 2007 straight
back to 1952 and starts again.

The year in the title is a frame variable. `labs()` text may embed `{...}`
expressions, glue-style, evaluated on every frame: `{closest_state}` is the year the
frame is nearest to, and it flips halfway through each move, at the same moment the
labels would if their text changed. `{previous_state}`, `{next_state}`,
`{transitioning}`, `{frame}` and `{progress}` are there too.

## Format

The output is an animated SVG. Ten bars, ten labels and an axis are a light scene, so
330 frames come to under 3 MB of markup, and because SVG is text it travels compressed:
under 100 KB over the wire. The same animation as a GIF is around 10 MB. A GIF is still
the choice when the animation must go somewhere that only takes images, such as a
slide or a chat message: `anim_save("race.gif", a)`.
